author: difficulty44_author_h

source_artifacts.claim: Current level defines STOP, STEADY, latched RESCUE, two owner-specific TARGET pads, a periodic sliding hall, powered/stabilized high bridge, three gates, two slime hazards, Cana core hazard, two owner-locked collectibles, and a boss requiring both target pads. Optional hint is assisted information.
Hold pads and latches apply gate, motor, power, and stabilize effects; boss target occupancy sets defeat; powered moving platforms cycle and stabilization stops their motion.
The defined STEADY and RESCUE pads each interrupt Cana's attack once; this cancels active projectiles and resets the attacker to cooldown.
Contact with the authored slime/core hazards or falling below world bounds kills a hero; both player-specific exits are needed, and boss presence also requires defeat.
Isp and Pac have distinct familiar movement/jump mappings, so simultaneous movement is supported without an extra interaction command.

prior_knowledge.concept: Basic movement, jumping, own-pad roles, and the shared both-exits goal.

evidence.claim: Opening room shows separate controls, pad ownership cues, and both matching exits.

prior_knowledge.concept: Riding and braking/powering a moving platform with a pad was introduced in Elevator Etiquette; here the moving hall and high bridge add periodic motion, stabilization, and a rescue latch.

evidence.claim: Prior intro says ride up and brake upstairs; moving-platform control is prior exposure, not mastery.

prior_knowledge.concept: Cana's boomerang can interfere with heroes, previously introduced as shove/float effects; interrupting the attack by activating control pads and using those same pads to restore/stabilize a route are new transfers.

evidence.claim: Prior intro explicitly frames Pac bating Cana's shove and Isp catching FLOAT, establishing attack-effect exposure only.

prior_knowledge.concept: Brain-fold/crossed-signal language was introduced earlier, but no earlier visible packet establishes the present STOP/STEADY/RESCUE route or two-target boss condition.

evidence.claim: Earlier cue names crossed brain signals and two brain folds.

mechanics.fact: Isp's STOP is a hold pad that stops the sliding hall and opens Pac's console gate; Pac's STEADY hold pad stabilizes the high bridge, powers the hall, opens Isp's high gate, and interrupts Cana once. Isp's RESCUE is a latch that opens both further gates, powers/stops the hall, stabilizes the bridge, and interrupts Cana once more.

evidence.claim: Level pad effects and barrier ownership are defined here.
The pads apply their hold/latch effects to motor, power, stabilization, and gates.
Each bound pad interrupts the configured attack once.

mechanics.fact: A validated route has Isp hold STOP while Pac rides the periodic hall to STEADY; that opens the high route. Isp releases STOP, boards the hall, crosses the console/high bridge, and latches RESCUE. Isp and Pac then occupy their owner-specific TARGET pads; both targets defeat Cana, and those positions also reach their matching exits.

evidence.claim: Current authored room geometry and pad/gate definitions support the route sequence; this is a legal demonstrated route, not proof of uniqueness.
Pac is on STEADY; its gate is open and high route is available while Isp initially held STOP.
Isp has latched RESCUE and both finish/high barriers are open.
Isp and Pac are simultaneously on their respective TARGET pads at their own exit regions.
Both matching exits are reached, status is complete, and deaths are zero.

mechanics.fact: The room has two lethal slime regions and an active Cana core hazard, plus boomerang-caused temporary dizzy/shove effects. A missed ferry is a periodic movement issue; it is not itself lethal. The target pads accept only their named hero, so a physical villain cannot substitute for either target contribution.

evidence.claim: Slime and villain-core hazards affect both; targets are owned by separate heroes and are required by the boss.
Hazard overlap is fatal.
Boomerang effects are temporary control changes, not direct lethal damage.

legal_routes.name: Stabilize and rescue the brain route, then occupy both targets/exits

steps.goal: Hold the hall still and open Pac's console access.
steps.action: Move right from spawn onto STOP and remain there while Pac boards the hall.
steps.expected_feedback: STOP disables hall motor and opens pac_console.
steps.observed_feedback: Production trace at frame 50 shows Isp occupying STOP and pac_console open.

evidence.claim: STOP is occupied by Isp and console gate is open.

steps.goal: Reach STEADY and restore the high bridge route.
steps.action: Ride/jump across the hall and console to the Pac-only STEADY pad; stay clear of the moat and Cana core.
steps.expected_feedback: STEADY stabilizes the bridge, powers the hall, opens isp_high, and interrupts one boomerang attack.
steps.observed_feedback: At frame 340 Pac occupies STEADY and Isp's high gate is open; the route continues with zero deaths.

evidence.claim: Steady is active and isp_high is open.
The hall is periodic and slime/core regions bound the route.

steps.goal: Cross the moving hall and console to latch RESCUE, permanently opening the remaining route.
steps.action: Leave STOP once Pac's STEADY has powered/opened the path, board the hall, jump onto the console and across the high bridge to Isp-only RESCUE.
steps.expected_feedback: RESCUE latches, opens pac_console, isp_high, and pac_finish, and interrupts Cana again.
steps.observed_feedback: By frame 700 RESCUE is latched and all route barriers are open.

evidence.claim: RESCUE is latched and the Pac finish gate is open.
RESCUE effects include latch, route gates, hall operation, and bridge stabilization.

steps.goal: Defeat Cana and finish by occupying both owned targets at the matching exits.
steps.action: Keep Isp on blue TARGET and guide Pac through the now-open finish gate to orange TARGET; avoid leaving the exposed routes before both are occupied.
steps.expected_feedback: Both owner-specific target pads become active, which defeats Cana; the target locations overlap their matched exits and both-exit completion follows.
steps.observed_feedback: At frame 942 both targets are occupied; the production replay completes at frame 943 with both exits and zero deaths.

evidence.claim: Both owned target pads are simultaneously occupied.
Both exits are reached and the level completes without death.
A current-source production replay demonstrates one legal both-exit route at 120 Hz; its route origin is historical and it is not a fresh44 human trial.

isp: Hold STOP to expose Pac's route; later ride the hall to Isp-only RESCUE and latch the upper/finish route; finally occupy Isp's blue TARGET at the matching exit.
The Isp-controlled route crosses the bridge/moat region and is exposed to Cana's dizzy effect if hit.
pac: Ride the ferry and hold Pac-only STEADY to stabilize/power the route, open Isp's high passage, and interrupt Cana once; then cross the open finish to Pac's orange TARGET/exit.
The Pac-controlled route is exposed to the moat and Cana's shove effect if hit.

common_mistakes.mistake: Isp leaves STOP before Pac has reached STEADY and opened the route.
common_mistakes.consequence: The hall becomes free to cycle and Pac's console access closes; the coordinated route is harder to recover but no immediate death is implied.
common_mistakes.recovery: Pac can continue riding the periodic hall and return to the necessary pad, while Isp can board on a subsequent cycle; exact restart cost is not tested. The intended route waits until STEADY is active before Isp departs.

evidence.claim: The hall is periodic and STEADY/RESCUE supply powered movement and route gates.
Hold effects change when the pad loses its owner; mover follows cycle/power state.

common_mistakes.mistake: Jumping short of the moving hall/high bridge or contacting a slime/core region while the route is not stabilized.
common_mistakes.consequence: A fall into either slime moat or the Cana core is lethal and can reset the attempt; temporary boomerang effects can also alter horizontal/jump response.
common_mistakes.recovery: The hall cycles and can be boarded again if the hero lands safely; rescue latches once reached. After a lethal hit the route must be retried, but no human restart or exact retry cost was measured.

evidence.claim: Periodic hall and bridge are adjacent to authored slime and villain hazards.
Lethal hazard contact sets game status dead.

optional_collectibles: Isp-owned blue spark at (850,330) and Pac-owned orange spark at (655,400); the initial HUD shows 0/2. Neither is required for the both-exits/boss objective.

reasoning.rationale: The pair must coordinate STOP, a moving hall, STEADY, a later RESCUE latch, two boomerang interruptions, and two target pads in order. Earlier rooms teach moving lifts and boomerang effects, but not the causal chain in which pads restore/interrupt the route. The production trace confirms that chain, not its first-encounter obviousness; first-pass 3 remains reasonable.

evidence.claim: Several distinct pad effects and target prerequisites must be sequenced.
A single validated schedule completes the ordered route but does not establish it is obvious or unique.

cooperation.rationale: The two heroes have distinct pad ownership: Isp holds STOP/RESCUE and blue TARGET; Pac holds STEADY and orange TARGET. Those roles open different gates, and both final target pads are required together to defeat Cana. This confirms and raises the first-pass 2 because cooperation is a hard mechanical dependency rather than merely suggested by separate labels.

evidence.claim: Owner-specific pads create distinct gate and boss-target contributions.
Both distinct target owners must occupy their pads simultaneously in the verified ending.

execution.rationale: The route has a cyclic ferry crossing, several jumps between platforms at different heights, pad occupancy while the partner advances, and an exposed slime/core region. The successful route avoids death, but this does not estimate player skill. First-pass null becomes 3 because concrete actions are known and require sustained two-character movement without extreme precision being established.

evidence.claim: Room geometry contains moving hall, console, bridge, low finish, gaps, and hazards.
The actions are executable in a deterministic route with zero deaths, but this does not measure human execution.

timing.rationale: The ferry has a ten-second cycle with seven seconds active, and pad effects change when the heroes step off. A pair must board and transfer at useful phases and activate the interrupt pads before later attack cycles. It is not a tight reflex test: the route can wait for the cycle and Rescue latches. This resolves first-pass null to moderate timing/state coordination.

evidence.claim: The ferry has a 10-second/7-second active cycle and STEADY powers it.
Pads interrupt attacks when activated; attacker then resumes its configured cooldown.

hazards.rationale: Two slime regions and Cana's core can kill either hero, and the mandatory route crosses the high bridge/ferry system beside those hazards. A validated zero-death route shows avoidance is possible, not that contact is harmless. Temporary dizzy/shove is kept separate from physical danger. First-pass null becomes 3 because hazards are real and route-relevant.

evidence.claim: Both slime regions and Cana core are authored as hazards harming both heroes.
Active hazard contact sets the run dead.

novelty.rationale: The first-pass 3 treated the signal-knot/boomerang combination as new. Earlier level 10 already introduced riding/braking a powered lift, and level 42 introduced boomerang-based hero interference; this room recombines those with pad-based interruption, bridge stabilization, a rescue latch, and two owner-specific boss targets. The transfer is still meaningful but no longer wholly unfamiliar.

evidence.claim: Moving lift and braking were introduced earlier.
Boomerang effect as a cooperative mechanic appeared earlier.
This room's combined stop/steady/rescue/target chain remains a new transfer.

recovery_cost.rationale: Missing the ferry or leaving a hold pad early is recoverable by waiting for the periodic hall or reactivating an accessible pad, and Rescue permanently latches the late route. A fall into slime/core is lethal and costs a fresh attempt, so mistakes have mixed but real consequence. No recovery route or human restart time was recorded; the score reflects source-supported mechanics, not measured retry burden.

evidence.claim: Ferry cycles and Rescue latches, but route hazards are lethal.
Pad occupancy can be re-established; periodic platforms keep cycling when powered.

solution_clarity.rationale: The screenshot names each pad, says Rescue stays on, and identifies the boomerang's player effects, which gives useful anchors. It does not state that STEADY and RESCUE interrupt Cana, that STOP enables Pac's first route, or that the late target pads defeat Cana. These are substantial causal steps supplied by the optional hint/source, not visible-first-encounter instruction. First-pass 3 remains appropriate despite the route now being known.

evidence.claim: The screenshot labels pads and effects but does not show their response or state transitions.
The optional hint teaches interrupt, restore, rescue, and target sequence not demonstrated in idle visuals.

control_friction.rationale: Unknown: the cited key mapping and scripted/native route evidence establish technical feasibility, but do not verify shared-keyboard two-human input reliability or a control defect. No browser keyboard-event reliability evidence is cited. Plausible risk only: Moving-platform/pad coordination belongs to cooperation/execution; the temporary boomerang response effect is intentional and belongs to execution.

evidence.claim: The controls are separately labeled for the two heroes.
Cana's boomerang can temporarily dizzy Isp or shove Pac.

confidence_reason: Current level source and a later deterministic production LEVELS trace confirm pad effects, route dependencies, lethal hazards, two-target defeat, and a zero-death clear. Confidence remains medium because the replay's route schedule is historical, not fresh44/human; no alternate-route enumeration, mistake recovery run, or human timing/control observation was performed, and optional hints are excluded from clarity claims.

confirmed: The visible labels correctly identify two control roles plus a rescue state and a signal/boomerang theme.
Both matching exits are mandatory; current source also makes both owner-specific target pads necessary to defeat Cana.
The room has a nontrivial shared route involving both heroes.
missed_mechanics: STOP holds the hall still and opens Pac's console gate; STEADY powers the hall, stabilizes the high bridge, opens Isp's high route, and interrupts Cana once.
RESCUE is a one-time latch that opens the remaining route and interrupts Cana a second time.
The periodic hall provides a retry opportunity, while slime and the Cana core create actual lethal consequences.
Two owner-specific target pads defeat Cana and coincide with the final exit positions.
incorrect_inferences: The first pass did not assert a specific causal mechanism as fact; its uncertainty about state persistence, timing, and route was proper for idle-only evidence.
changed_judgments: Cooperation rose from 2 to 3 because source and trace show owner-specific STOP/STEADY/RESCUE progression and simultaneous owned boss targets are mechanically required, not merely suggested by labels.
Execution changed from null to 3 because the legal route is now known: ferry traversal, jumps, maintained pads, and split target approaches; source/route does not provide a human success rate.
Timing changed from null to 2 because the hall cycles and boomerang interruptions create sequencing, although waiting and a latched rescue avoid narrow reaction deadlines.
Hazards changed from null to 3 because two slime areas and Cana core lethally harm both heroes on the route; the clear only proves avoidance is possible.

Novelty fell from 3 to 2 because level 10 previously taught riding/braking a lift and level 42 taught boomerang interference; pad-triggered interruptions plus rescue/targets are a new combination, not wholly new mechanics.
Recovery cost changed from null to 2 because the periodic hall and reactivatable hold states permit some correction, while falls into lethal hazards cost an attempt; no human reset timing is claimed.

Solution clarity stays 3: visible labels are helpful, but the crucial interrupt, bridge/power, and two-target boss causal chain is not demonstrated in the idle screenshot and the optional hint supplies assistance.

At 2026-10-17T17:51:21Z, the paired control-friction estimate was withdrawn from 2 to unknown: available source mappings and scripted/native input traces establish feasibility, not shared-keyboard two-human input reliability or control failure. Plausible coordination, execution, and intentional movement-effect concerns remain qualitative risks in their own dimensions.
unresolved: Whether a novice infers the STOP→STEADY→RESCUE chain and interrupt effects from visible labels without optional hint; no human attempt was observed.
Whether any alternate route avoids one of the intermediate pads while still reaching both targets/exits; the traced schedule is not exhaustive.
Exact retry cost after lethal fall, actual human timing/execution reliability, control comfort, fun, and first-encounter difficulty.
Whether target occupancy defeats Cana immediately in a perceived/visible way; the deterministic route establishes completion state but not player-facing feedback quality.

single_operator_note: The two-human baseline assigns the distinct pads to different people. One operator must switch attention between Isp and Pac while one waits on STOP/STEADY and the other boards the ferry, later guide Isp across to RESCUE, and coordinate both target arrivals. This divided attention is additional to the two-human ratings and has not been measured.
